Frontend hosting: projects, deployments, domains and logs through the Vercel REST API.

## API key

- **Get your key here:** [vercel.com](https://vercel.com/account/tokens)
- **Setting:** `VERCEL_API_TOKEN`
- **API reference:** [vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api)

### Get the key

1. Sign in to Vercel and open [vercel.com](https://vercel.com/account/tokens).
2. Create an API key (or token) with only the access your apps need.
3. Copy it. Many providers show a key only once.

**What to create:** An access token from your account's Tokens page, sent as a bearer token; scope it to one team or one project. A team- or project-scoped token needs no teamId parameter.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Vercel) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set VERCEL_API_TOKEN
```

It asks for the value at a hidden prompt, and it's live at once, with no deploy. If an app you've installed needs it, `pnpm everyapp configure <app>` asks for it along with everything else the app needs.

### Use it in an app

List it in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
capabilities: {
  vercel: { access: "read", why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

`access` is `"read"` (or `"write"` where it changes things). The app calls the provider's own URLs with `integrationFetch()`, and the Gateway adds the key. More in [API providers](/docs/agent/providers).

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show vercel` shows the key as set and which apps use it.
- `pnpm everyapp status` shows apps that were waiting for it as ready.
- To test the key itself, `GET https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects` with it should answer 200; the call is free.

### Cost and limits

- **Rate limits:** Limits are per action (deployments, domains, teams), listed on Vercel's limits page.
